Packed decoders consume eight coexisting compressed-u32 data items word7..word0 and return either sixteen centered limbs limb15..limb0 or fifty-one biased digits digit50..digit0. Both decoder variants require zero auxiliary hints per invocation and across the G32 schedule's 46 grouped and 47 digit invocations. The preserved-item argument counts unrelated combined main/altstack state; decoder-local peaks include their sixteen temporary script-authored powers.

records.name: Fast base-16 Winternitz signatures
records.summary: Tapscript-specialized Winternitz with typed HASH160, SHA-256, or SHA-256 chains/HASH160 commitments, default 16-byte initial secrets, canonical-bit and strided terminal profiles, narrow full-table numeric lookups, measured onchain costs, and consuming keys.
records.security: Strictly one-time classic unkeyed hash-chain Winternitz, not WOTS+; durable seed-reuse prevention remains a caller obligation. Bitwise profiles bind canonical false/true items through tapscript MINIMALIF; numeric profiles do not bind raw in-range ScriptNum serialization. Explicit clamped profiles also accept above-range raw digits as their authenticated chain maximum, matching legacy saturation semantics; strict profiles retain upper rejection. Size profiles accept arbitrary-length selected-hash preimages whenever at least one hash executes; for Sha256Hash160 this includes the maximum digit due to the final commitment hash, while FullWidth signer nodes are native width (20/32 bytes); Preimage16 signer nodes and strict profiles use 16 bytes iff digit zero and native width otherwise. Idealized single-target classical preimage/collision bounds are 160/80 and 256/128 bits respectively, not end-to-end Winternitz security claims; multi-target and chain losses remain unquantified. The hash choice is bound to key types and separate derivation domains, not chosen by the witness. Preimage16 limits initial-secret exhaustive search to at most 128 single-target classical bits before multi-target effects; this is a security tradeoff, not proof of 128-bit Winternitz security. It does not raise HASH160 collision resistance. The preimage mode has a separate derivation namespace and is carried in key types. Sha256Hash160 binds a separate key derivation domain and retains 20-byte commitments with an 80-bit idealized generic collision bound. The strided profile uses canonical b=1-(digit mod 2) and upper-clamped q=floor(digit/2); the same authenticated digit 2*min(q,max/2)+1-b enters the weighted checksum. Above-range q aliases one of the last two chain digits. There is no new end-to-end security proof.
records.stack_contract: For 32-byte messages, numeric witnesses contain 134 items and measured lookup peaks are 143; strided terminal witnesses contain 201 items and peak at 209; bitwise witnesses contain 333 items and peak at 334 for recovery or 333 for terminal verification. All profiles require zero auxiliary hint items and all data items coexist at entry. Recovery profiles return 64 message nibbles; terminal profiles clear signature state and require a terminal predicate. Count surrounding main/altstack state against the same 1,000-item ceiling.

records.summary: Reversible 160-bit encoding into 41 mixed-radix digits (32 radix-16, four radix-18, five radix-20) summing to 321; terminal verification uses a whole-vector anti-forwarding relation to omit individual upper bounds. records.security: One-time classic unkeyed Winternitz, not WOTS+. Requires honest independent key derivation, canonical signer codewords, and durable seed-reuse prevention. Encoding is injective over all unchanged 20-byte messages; no hashing, padding search, or message grinding. The unbounded terminal relation may admit an overflow selector that reads outside its own table. Such a coordinate exceeds any honest signed digit; any distinct tuple with the exact same sum must decrease another coordinate, which still selects inside its own chain table and requires inversion/collision. This is a local whole-vector argument, not a formal WOTS+ proof or local radix validation. Negative indices and oversized ScriptNums fail by Script rules; arithmetic does not wrap. Bounded terminal mode explicitly rejects upper-range selectors. Both modes omit raw node-width checks. Initial-secret search is capped at 128 single-target classical bits before multi-target losses. HASH160 and hybrid commitments retain 80-bit generic collision bounds; pure SHA256 has 128. Host decoding rejects rank>=2^160, while Script does not enforce that image boundary.
records.stack_contract: HASH160 uses 82 signature data items [node,digit] and peaks at 93 combined items. SHA256 and hybrid use 123 items [quotient,node,canonical bit] and peak at 133. No auxiliary hints; all data coexist at entry.
